newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal says any single currency delay dangerous.
newsitem.headline: Portugal says any single currency delay dangerous.

text.p: Failure to launch the single currency on time in 1999 would be a dangerous setback to the European Union, Portuguese Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco warned on Wednesday.
Sousa Franco said the European Union had committed itself so strongly to economic and monetary union (EMU) that delay would inevitably be seen as a blow to the whole concept of European unity.
"Failure in this challenge would be a failure for the whole European project," he said in a speech to the American Club of Lisbon.
"Either Europe is successful (in launching EMU) or it takes a dangerous step backwards," he said.
Portugal's Socialist government has staked its credibility on being among the pioneers of the single currency and its policies have been aimed at meeting the economic tests for entry.
Sousa Franco, a political independent who formerly headed the country's court of accounts, said that monetary union would inevitably involve some form of budgetary and fiscal federalism.
Taking the example of the United States, Sousa Franco said that it was not possible to have monetary union without some centralising of budgetary issues and a degree of harmonisation in tax matters.
"The need for (some) common budget is written in the stars and cannot be avoided," he said.
